# Public syntax/build checks
The external public evaluator parses Python/JavaScript/Vue/TypeScript source or checks Go/PHP/Ruby syntax / compiles public Java sources. These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations. Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task:
# Task

The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready. Update the file download dialog so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status.

limitations: TASK does not specify retry delay, backoff, attempt limits, scheduler failures, or rejected preparation checks.
The public dialog flow represents delivery readiness through completed; the actual file-delivery mechanism is not supplied.
The dialog-specific discard policy must not be transferred to src/useBackgroundPreparation.js, whose source says: "Closing this progress panel does not cancel workspace-owned work."

rules.body: Apply this guidance when a service distinguishes pending from ready and the observer must poll before delivery. TASK states: "The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready" and "keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status."

Capture the token and lifecycle identity when starting a check. After PREPARATION_STATUS.PENDING resolves, schedule another check for that same identity while preserving loading; before either the resolved callback or scheduled callback mutates state, verify that the observer is active and that both lifecycle and token are still current.

On PREPARATION_STATUS.READY, cancel any scheduled retry, clear loading, record the token at most once, and publish the updated snapshot. Preserve the immediate first check and the immediate check performed after reopen assigns its next token.

Invalidate the dialog lifecycle and cancel its retry at discard boundaries such as close, reopen replacement, and unmount so old results cannot affect a later dialog lifecycle. Do not impose this policy on workspace-owned background work, which has a different ownership boundary.

Verify at least pending→ready and repeated-pending→ready sequences, checking that completion occurs only after ready, loading remains active while pending, checkCount advances for each actual check, retries cease after ready, completion is not duplicated, and late results or retries from closed, replaced, or unmounted lifecycles are ignored.

checkpoints: After start or reopen initiates a check, interpret the resolved preparation status using PREPARATION_STATUS.
When the status is PENDING, keep the dialog in a waiting/loading state and arrange another check for the same preparation lifecycle.
When the status is READY, stop further retries, clear loading, record completion for the applicable token, and publish the updated snapshot.
At close, reopen, token change, and component unmount boundaries, verify whether outstanding requests or scheduled retries remain valid for the current dialog lifecycle.
forbidden_effects: Do not mark a token completed or deliver its file while the preparation service reports PENDING.
Do not weaken the existing immediate first check performed by start or reopen.
Do not apply a stale asynchronous result or retry to a different token or reopened dialog lifecycle.
Do not introduce duplicate completion records or continue retrying after READY.
Do not change the workspace-owned background export behavior merely to implement dialog polling.
Do not modify tests or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: A polling lifecycle is identified by the download-dialog hook instance together with the token whose preparation is being checked.
reopen(nextToken) establishes a visible dialog lifecycle for nextToken and immediately begins checking it.
An asynchronous result or scheduled retry belongs to the token/lifecycle that created it, even if state.current.token later changes.
Closing, reopening, token switching, and unmounting are distinct boundaries whose intended cancellation behavior must not be conflated.

obligations.text: The file download dialog must continue checking when preparation resolves to PREPARATION_STATUS.PENDING.
The dialog must record completion and enable file delivery only after preparation resolves to PREPARATION_STATUS.READY.
A pending result must preserve the active waiting/loading behavior until a later ready result completes that token.
Polling must retain the dialog's existing start and reopen behavior, including the immediate check and observable checkCount updates.
Retries and asynchronous results must remain associated with the token and dialog lifecycle that initiated them, and must not create duplicate completion or post-ready polling.
The background preparation panel's documented workspace-owned continuation behavior must remain unchanged because the requested change is scoped to the file download dialog.

ordering_barriers: A resolved PENDING status must precede scheduling the next check; it must not pass through the READY completion path.
READY must be observed before completion is recorded or the file is considered deliverable.
Any scheduled retry must re-check preparation before completion can be recorded.
The immediate check initiated by reopen(nextToken) occurs after assigning nextToken and making the dialog visible.
Lifecycle/token validity must be established before an asynchronous result mutates dialog state.
preservation: Preserve the public preparation status meanings: false is pending and true is ready.
Preserve start as an immediate preparation check that sets loading, increments checkCount, and publishes state.
Preserve close making the download dialog invisible.
Preserve reopen assigning the next token, making the dialog visible, publishing, and immediately checking.
Preserve snapshot isolation for completed by returning a copied array.
Preserve BackgroundExportPanel/useBackgroundPreparation behavior, including continued workspace-owned work after its panel closes.
Preserve the public component surface and data-visible/data-loading rendering behavior.
scope: Business-code changes are limited to the file download dialog preparation flow, principally src/usePreparation.js and only supporting public business code if necessary.
The behavior in scope begins when DownloadDialog's preparation API starts or reopens a token and ends when that token becomes ready or its lifecycle is invalidated.
Tests and configuration are outside the edit scope.

supporting_evidence.quote: The preparation service can now report that a file is still pending before it becomes ready.
Update the file download dialog so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the file only after a ready status.
// transport resolves false while preparation is pending and true when ready.
// Closing this progress panel does not cancel workspace-owned work.

triggers: Calling the download dialog preparation API's start method.
Calling reopen(nextToken), which immediately invokes a preparation check.
Execution of a retry scheduled after a pending result.
Closing, reopening, switching token, or unmounting while a request or retry is outstanding.
unknowns: The public sources do not expose the actual file-delivery mechanism; completed is the only visible readiness/completion record in the supplied dialog hook.
The task does not specify retry delay, backoff, maximum attempts, or error handling; the public scheduler API supplies timing externally.

The task does not explicitly state whether closing the download dialog cancels its polling, unlike the explicit background-panel comment; existing observable behavior and lifecycle safety must guide that boundary.
The supplied DownloadDialog passes token only as the hook's initial value, so behavior for a prop-only token change without reopen is not specified.
The public sources do not define rejection behavior for checkPreparation or failures in retry scheduling/cancellation.
Only the acceptance verdict is available for feedback; no failure cause inferred.

change_summary: Added independent reusable guidance for lifecycle-bound polling because the frozen experience catalog and related experiences contain no existing entry to revise or merge.

The new guidance covers retained immediate start/reopen checks, pending retry scheduling, ready-only deduplicated completion, token/lifecycle validation, dialog discard boundaries, and preservation of the separate workspace-owned background policy.
reflection_update.reason: Attempt 1 passed acceptance and demonstrates a reusable async polling mechanism with captured token/lifecycle identity, scheduled retries for PENDING, READY-only completion, and stale-continuation rejection. No existing guidance is available as a lineage target; this is not merely a wording or case-identity variant.
